text:
maya: quick heads-up — planning to enable flashattn v3 behind a feature flag for paged-attn heavy workloads tomorrow. want to run a focused preflight: batching heuristics smoke, KV-cache hit/regressions, and a few fused-attn microbenchmarks. cc @dmitri @kevin

 dmitri: sg. can you enumerate the specific checks? i can script the perf CI jobs. key things: latency tail, p50/p95 tokens/sec, kv hit-rate delta, and a sanity regression for quality (few eval prompts). also verify fallback to v2 if kernel fails.

 maya: checklist i had in mind: 
 - run 1k warmup requests with mixed seq (64/256/1024)
 - run continuous batching at target qps (100 req/s) for 10m
 - check kv cache evictions and hit-rate by session id
 - compare kernel selection logs (v2 vs v3)
 - validate streaming correctness (no token drops)
 - run fused-attn microbench for fused vs non-fused path

 kevin: i'll add a smoke that toggles the feature flag per shard and exercises the fallback policy. propose flag: `runtime.attn.flash_v3.enable=true/false` and per-model override: `model.config.attn_kernel=auto|flashv2|flashv3|paged`

 ashwin: throwing in a quick perf note — v3 tends to shine at seq>=512 due to tiled kernels, but we saw some 3-7% regressions at seq<128 with certain attention fusion settings. also need to watch memory transient spikes with KV prefetch.

 perf-ci-bot: perf-smoke (1749771250) finished: 
 ```
 scenario: mixed-seq-1k-warmup
 flash_v3:on p50=12.4ms p95=45.1ms tokens/s=1750
 flash_v3:off p50=11.8ms p95=44.7ms tokens/s=1790
 delta tokens/s = -2.2% (regression)
 kv_hit_rate:on = 0.87 kv_hit_rate:off = 0.88
 memory_peak_delta = +120MB
 ```

 dmitri: ugh that delta is small but real. can we get a per-seq breakdown? might be caused by batching heuristics not selecting tiled batch sizes for small seq.

 perf-ci-bot: per-seq breakdown attached (summaries): 
 ```
 seq64: flash_v3 tokens/s -5.8%
 seq256: flash_v3 tokens/s -1.0%
 seq1024: flash_v3 tokens/s +6.9%
 ```

 kevin: ok that aligns with expectations. mitigation plan: 1) add a quick heuristic to prefer v2 for seq<=96 unless model requests paged/fused. 2) tweak batching policy: cap cross-batch fusion for small seq to avoid kernel overhead. 3) increase KV prefetch throttle to avoid spikes.

 maya: agree. for rollout gating, propose phased enablement: 
 - phase 0: flag=false default, internal-only quota buckets test on dedicated pool 
 - phase 1: flag=true for dedicated-only low-traffic shards (5% of capacity) with automatic rollback on >3% token/s regression or >2% kv hit drop 
 - phase 2: wider rollout with canary on hosted for models known to benefit (long-seq chat)

 ashwin: also add telemetry keys: `attn.kernel_selected`, `attn.seq_len`, `attn.kv_hit`, `attn.batch_size`, `attn.fallback_reason`. that'll let runtime pick regressions quickly.

 dmitri: will implement the kernel selector change. rough pseudo for selector rules: 
 ```
 if model.config.attn_kernel == 'flashv3': choose flashv3
 else if seq_len >= 512 and mem_avail > threshold: choose flashv3
 else if seq_len <= 96: choose flashv2
 else: choose auto (bench heuristics based on rolling perf stats)
 ```

 kevin: i can wire the feature flag and gating logic in console with alert hooks. alert thresholds: tokens/s drop 3% sustained over 5m OR p95 latency +20% over baseline OR kv_hit drop 2% absolute.

 maya: for QA: please run the eval set of 200 prompts for correctness (token-stream diffs) — want to ensure v3 doesn't change decoding order or NAR behaviour for fused-attn.

 perf-ci-bot: decode-diff check (1749771288): 200 prompts => 0 diffs (token stream identical)

 ashwin: nice. so functional parity seems ok. biggest risk is perf for short sequences + memory spikes. we should be conservative: default to v2 for low-latency short seq models (embedding endpoints, completion short prompts).

 dmitri: action items: 
 - i'll land selector heuristics and unit tests (ETA today EOD)
 - kevin: console flag + rollback hooks (ETA tomorrow AM)
 - maya: schedule dedicated-canary run and monitor (ETA tomorrow afternoon)
 - ashwin: tune KV prefetch throttle and run memory regression tests (ETA tomorrow)

 maya: thanks all. i'll post a short runbook in #eng-runtime before flipping any shard. if anyone sees unexpected rollbacks, ping me and we'll hotfix selector to force v2 for the impacted model. :rocket:

 kevin: added alert dashboard and auto-rollback policy. will label the canary shards `flashv3-canary-1/2`.

 perf-ci-bot: follow-up regression job queued (1749771299).

 maya: closing thread — will update with canary results. :eyes:
